sentences.text:
In Re:- Narayan Maity vs Re: An Application For Bail Under ... on
24 June, 2016
Author: Ashim Kumar Roy

Bench: Ashim Kumar Roy
 1
69 24.6.2016
pd. C.R.M. No. 4820 of 2016 In re:- Narayan Maity ... Petitioner.

-And- 
Re: An application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. affirmed on 11.5.2016 in connection with
Moyna Police Station Case No.228/2015 dated 28.9.2015 under Sections 272/273 of the Indian
Penal Code read with West Bengal Act 42 of 1973, Section 3/304/120B of the Indian Penal Code and
Section 46Aa of the Bengal Excise Act and Section 16(3) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
Mr. Deep Chaim Kabir, Mr. Subhas Jana ... For the petitioner.
Mr. Manjit Singh, P.P., Mr. Partha Pratim Das .... For the State.
Heard the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the parties.
The petitioner is in custody for 8  months and out of nine chargesheeted-accused persons, two are on bail.

The learned Counsel for the petitioner in his usual fairness submits that he never claimed that this petitioner is standing on the same footing with the other co-accused, who were granted bail by this Court.
We have been informed by the learned Public Prosecutor that already charge has been framed and on and from June 28, 2016, the trial is going to be commenced.
It is his further submission that this is a case of consumption of spurious and poisonous country liquor and as a result thereof, total 23 persons died.

We have gone through the case diary and considering the nature and seriousness of the allegation and petitioner's involvement in the commission of the offence, in our opinion, this is not a fit case for bail.
Accordingly, the application for bail stands rejected at this stage.
